reproduction_target: Three simulation studies on inferring negative frequency-dependent selection (NFDS) from time-sampled/ancient-DNA data: (1) allele-frequency trajectory simulations distinguishing recent NFDS from partial selective sweeps; (2) forward simulations of population contraction to separate selective effects from population history via SFS/variation changes over time; (3) an ABC approach comparing multiple- vs single-timepoint power for estimating the duration T_b over which NFDS has shaped variation. All data are simulated; single-author perspective paper.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool from Methods prose of the bioRxiv preprint (JATS XML abstract + Methods extracted; full XML re-fetch was Cloudflare rate-limited (HTTP 1015) mid-assessment, but the SLiM/libsequence method paragraphs, Data availability, and Acknowledgements were captured before the block). GitHub repo file tree + README prose read to confirm artifact set (SLiM .slim scripts, R ABC scripts, python summary-stats script, jupyter plotting notebook, and bundled simulated-data tarballs). No workflow source read at line level (stage1). Pure-computational: no wet-lab steps, W=0.

steps.label: SLiM v4.2.3 forward-in-time simulations (equilibrium population w/ beneficial mutation on neutral background; allele-frequency trajectories for NFDS vs selective sweep vs overdominance; population-contraction demography; parameters from human inferences, 100 replicates per regime)

Summary-statistic calculation via the python implementation of libsequence (pylibseq) v1.8.3 (Tajima's D, haplotype diversity, r^2; 10kb sliding windows, 5kb step; means/SD across windows and replicates)

Approximate Bayesian Computation inference in R (scripts ABC_multiple_timepoints.R / ABC_single_timepoint.R) to estimate T_b and compare multiple- vs single-timepoint power — no R version and no ABC package/version stated in prose
Figure generation via jupyter notebook plot_figures.ipynb (python) from bundled summary-statistic tarballs — no version/env stated
